Subject: Re: Security exhibit language / inspection window

Marcus / Laura —

Thanks for sending the draft earlier. A couple of asks from our side as we start legal review:

- Can we narrow the pen-test staging access language to "scoped, timeboxed, and read-only unless otherwise agreed"? Our infosec is nervous about broad forensic access.
- Novamed prefers an evidence cadence that avoids weekly pull requests — would you accept quarterly sampled evidence plus an annual full evidence handoff for SOC 2?
- We need clarity on responsibility for gathering logs vs. metadata exports (who owns the runbook and who is responsible for retrieval).

I've attached our annotated exhibit (security-exhibit-novamed-comments.pdf) and an internal checklist. If you can confirm a proposed rules-of-engagement doc and a point person for evidence collection, we can escalate to our GC.

Thanks —
Sabrina Wu
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager, Novamed

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-20T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit language / inspection window

Sabrina — appreciate the clear notes. High level response and proposed 'rules of engagement' below. See attached evidence matrix and a lightweight process doc.

Proposed rules of engagement (summary):
- Notice: 30 days written notice for scheduled inspections or pen tests; 72 hours notice for urgent security incident sampling.
- Scope: Limit pen-test staging access to agreed hostnames/IPs and specific service tiers; no broad forensic access or live DB queries unless a separate SOW is executed and both sides sign a limited-access addendum.
- Evidence cadence: Quarterly sampled exports (config + metadata + logs for sampled time windows) + an annual consolidated evidence package for SOC 2 review. We propose a weekly digest e-mail only for high-priority findings, not for routine exports.
- Ownership: Redwood will own the retrieval runbook for platform-side artifacts; customer (Novamed) will own application-layer logs unless we are operating under Dedicated/Private where we can provide a consolidated bundle. We'll capture responsibilities in the attached matrix.
- Pen-test windows: Tests run in staging by default; production testing requires a risk review and an approved change window.
- NDAs & truncated retention: All inspection attendees must sign an inspection NDA; snapshots provided for evidence are retained 90 days unless otherwise specified in the order form.

Next steps: Laura / Kimberly — can you review the suggested clause language in the attached redline and confirm whether the 30-day notice and 90-day retention are acceptable or should be escalated to Sales for a concession (credits or surcharge).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-08-20T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit language / inspection window (legal redline notes)

Team — I reviewed Marcus's proposed rules and Novamed's comments. A few legal redline suggestions to keep the commercial relationship and audit rights balanced: 

1) Narrow inspection triggers: change "inspection for any reason" to "inspection where customer demonstrates a legitimate compliance need or in response to a material security incident".
2) Scope carveout: limit forensics to systems strictly in scope of the order form; require separate written consent for any expanded access.
3) Evidence retention: retain platform-provided snapshots 90 days; provide a one-time archival package for SOC 2 upon request at mutually agreed cost/reasonable notice.
4) Confidentiality: add explicit inspection NDA language and a clause that forbids customer from attempting to rehost or redistribute raw snapshot contents.

Suggested insertion to the exhibit (example language):
"Customer inspection rights shall be limited to the control families outlined in Exhibit A and shall be triggered only upon (i) scheduled audit with prior 30-day notice, (ii) regulatory obligation, or (iii) a material security incident where disclosure is required. Forensic access to live systems requires a discrete SOW and express written approval from Redwood's security lead."

I attached a tracked-change version of the exhibit and a short memo for the commercial team on negotiating cost for archival evidence. Marcus / Kimberly — please incorporate the redline text into your operational matrix and confirm whether the 30-day/90-day defaults are acceptable or should be escalated to Sales for a concession (credits or surcharge).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachment: msa-orderform-redline_trackchanges.docx (DOCX, tracked changes)

Laura / Marcus — thanks, that helps clarify. A couple quick responses from Novamed Legal: 

- We can accept the 30-day notice for scheduled audits and the 90-day retention for provided snapshots, conditional on a one-time SOC 2 archival package for our next audit. Please include a line item (estimate) in the order form for archival retrieval.
- Please remove the phrase "broad forensic access" from any interim language — we still need firm limits that prohibit live DB queries unless signed SOW.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Wednesday 8/27 at 10:00 PT to finalize language and confirm the line item?
